subject: Intermittent POST failures after private peering cutover — AS_PATH/MTU investigation
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-logistics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, netops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: POSTs to on-prem backend failing after peering cutover

Ben —

We cut over to the new private peering with FastLink overnight and are seeing intermittent failures for large POSTs to our on-prem ingestion endpoint. The failures pop up as 502s at the LB layer; when we grab tcpdump on the on-prem edge we see repeated retransmits and occasional ICMP frag-needed messages that look like PMTU-related.

What we've done so far:
- Re-routed traffic to legacy path and failures stop.
- TCP dumps attached (acme_pcap_20261124.pcap).
- Traceroutes from client and from our edge included in the capture.

Notes: the FastLink peering team confirmed they are doing an AS_PATH rewrite for transit aggregation (they said it was temporary). We suspect either PMTU blackholing or something in the transit rewrite interacting with an on-prem NAT. Can you advise next steps? This is impacting a small subset of file uploads and one of our scheduled batch jobs.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
NetOps Lead — Acme Logistics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POSTs to on-prem backend failing after peering cutover

Alice — thanks for the data and quick repro notes. We've pulled the pcap and started an initial triage. High-level hypotheses:

1) PMTU blackhole caused by MTU reduction on the new transit path + lack of MSS clamp on the SVG/edge NAT. Large POSTs trigger TCP segments that exceed an intermediate MTU and DF=1 prevents fragmentation; hosts don't receive proper ICMP frag-needed in some paths.
2) AS_PATH rewriting by FastLink may be changing next-hop selection on one of the upstream ASes which pushes traffic through a device that performs SNAT/port normalization and causes packet size/translation anomalies.

Action items (what we'll try next):
- Soojin: can you check our border NAT config (SNAT/port-preserve, conntrack timeouts) and whether the edge applies MSS clamp? If not, add a temporary MSS clamp and test.
- Jordan: can you run controlled PMTU/probe tests from our edge to the on-prem IPs (iperf with varied MSS/DF flags) and share outputs.
- Marissa: please coordinate with Acme's FastLink contact (cc'd noc) to ask them to temporarily remove AS_PATH rewrite or enable AS-override-like behavior for the specific prefix space so we can validate routing differences.

I've attached our trace log (redwood_trace_log_20261125.txt) with timestamps and the connection IDs that match the pcap. Will follow up as soon as we have results.

Ben Carter
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POSTs to on-prem backend failing after peering cutover

Ben / Alice — quick triage notes from the edge/NAT perspective after running a few tests this morning:

What I see:
- Our eBPF/conntrack logs show repeated SYNs with MSS 1460 where later segments are ~1500 bytes (DF=1). We see occasional ICMP "frag needed" retransmissions but they don't always surface to the originator — classic PMTU blackhole signature.
- Border device (rtr-pe-01) is not currently applying an MSS clamp for TCP path stabilization.
- SNAT is enabled with port-preserve disabled for the Acme tenant; ephemeral port reuse looks fine for normal traffic but large flows can trigger different translation paths in the transit ring.
- BGP adj across FastLink shows AS_PATH modifications; when we force our next-hop selection to prefer the legacy path the problem disappears.

Immediate mitigations applied (for controlled test window only):
- Enabled MSS clamp 1400 on rtr-pe-01 outbound to Acme prefixes (temporary).
- Temporarily pinned route selection to legacy transit for the affected prefixes.

Results: after MSS clamp was applied we saw successful large POSTs in repeated iperf/filesize tests. When we remove the clamp and force the FastLink path again, failures return.

Longer-term recommendations:
- Ask FastLink to stop AS_PATH rewriting for these prefixes (or expose AS-override/next-hop-self semantics) while we validate path behavior. AS_PATH rewrite is changing route selection and likely steering traffic through a PE that enforces different MTU/translation behavior.
- Consider making MSS clamp permanent for this tenant or enable PMTU probing/ICMP reflection policy with the provider to avoid blackholing.
- Revisit SNAT port-preserve for Acme tenant if there are multiple egress devices doing asymmetric translation.

Jordan — please paste iperf/test outputs here when ready and we'll compare sequence/ack patterns.

Soojin Lee
Senior Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-logistics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Transit Provider NOC <noc@fastlink-transit.net>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POSTs to on-prem backend failing after peering cutover

Team — quick update from our end: FastLink acknowledged the issue and temporarily removed the AS_PATH aggregation for the Acme prefixes and engaged their PE team to adjust MTU handling. After FastLink's change + Redwood's MSS clamp we ran a 6-hour batch window with large uploads; no errors.

FastLink's note: they found an intermediate PE doing aggressive MTU enforcement when AS_PATH was rewritten (they've pushed a firmware tweak to honor ICMP frag-needed and are rolling the change).

Next steps:
- We'll keep Redwood's MSS clamp enabled for 48 hours as a safety net, then remove for a test during a low-traffic window.
- Schedule a short postmortem (INF-4821) to capture root cause and remediation steps.
- Marissa — can you confirm whether we should propose a change to our standard peering runbook (avoid AS_PATH rewrite for private peering) and update the contract notes?

Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Alice Chen
NetOps Lead — Acme Logistics
